tasks.short: Select stone-carving tools and their sequence of use

steps.what: Select chisels, pneumatic tools, surfacing tools or sandblasting nozzles and determine their sequence

tasks.design: Retain tool and sequence selection with the carver, consulting job references in {DOCS}. Selection depends on the actual stone and intended result; a catalogue does not provide a complete decision rule.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tool suitability varies with stone condition, shape and desired finish.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing job references support experienced physical assessment.
tasks.still_hard: Choose a sequence that achieves the form without damaging the material.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise stone behaviour and adapt tool choice.

evidence.claim: Physical stone assessment and tool-sequence judgement retain full time; no structured automatic selection contract is established.

assumptions: The baseline is tool selection rather than catalogue data entry.
The carver assesses material condition during s1; no free material-quality flag is assumed.
No new automation service or added upkeep is introduced.
research_questions: Do existing tool references resolve repeated questions without extra material capture?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Material assessment and tool sequencing remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Study artistic references and plan carving or cutting techniques

steps.what: Study artistic objects, models, sketches or blueprints to plan carving or cutting techniques

tasks.design: Keep artistic interpretation and technique planning with the carver using physical references and {DOCS}. Digitising a sketch does not establish that the intended form or workable cutting approach can be inferred without skilled assessment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Artistic intent and physical constraints must be reconciled for each object.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing models and drawings provide reference information.
tasks.still_hard: Translate a form into feasible cuts while respecting the stone.
tasks.human_edge: Combine visual judgement with knowledge of material behaviour.
tasks.altitude: Own the relationship between artistic intent and physical technique.

reach.task: Clarify intended form and acceptable variation

evidence.claim: Interpretation of artistic references and physical technique planning retain full time in this design.

assumptions: The baseline is reference study and technique planning; detailed tool selection is counted in its separate task.
No repeated geometric transcription burden is invented from the task statement.
No new automated service or maintenance is added.
unknowns: Reference formats and repeated geometric work
research_questions: Are there repeated geometric calculations separable from artistic and material judgement?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Artistic study and technique planning remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain material judgement and artistic interpretation in stone carving.
reach: Clarify finish requirements with quality technicians
role.ambitious_version: A stone carver who uses existing references while retaining skilled decisions about form, material and technique.
